resources.string: Sunteţi sigur că doriţi să dezinstalaţi aplicaţiile %1$s?
Canta places a small helper in /data/local/tmp on the device to read and manage apps. It runs only while Canta uses it.
This device runs an Android version older than 9, which Canta doesn\'t support.
Couldn\'t set up Canta\'s helper on the device. Check that it is connected and authorized, then try again.
Failed to reach the device. Check that it is connected and authorized.

CANTA este o aplicație open source de dezinstalare care folosește Shizuku pentru a elimina aplicațiile de sistem și utilizator. Îți permite să îți deblochezi dispozitivul așa cum dorești, nu este necesar un calculator.

Mulțumiri speciale %1$s.
CANTA nu ar fi la fel fără munca lor.
Preluați automat informațiile despre aplicațiile nedorite. Acest lucru garantează existența actualizării insignelor si a descrierii aplicațiilor.

Această aplicație oferă recomandări de eliminare a aplicațiilor bazate pe informații despre terți. Aceste recomandări sunt de natură informativă și nu garantează siguranța sau compatibilitatea cu dispozitivul dvs. specific. Dezinstalarea aplicațiilor de sistem poate cauza probleme neașteptate, inclusiv, dar nelimitându-se la: pierderea funcționalității, instabilitatea sistemului, bootloop-uri ale dispozitivului, pierderea datelor etc. Dezvoltatorul acestei aplicații nu este responsabil pentru nicio defecțiune efectuată pe dispozitiv ca urmare a recomandărilor furnizate.
Apăsând pe \"Proceed\", sunteți de acord să folosiți această aplicație pe propriul risc.
Dacă se afişează dialogul pentru confirmarea acțiunii de dezinstalare.
Apăsați %1$d de mai multe ori pentru a activa toate funcționalitățile.
Selectați tot ce a fost activat pentru tipul de filtru \"Recomandat\".
Import a preset from clipboard or paste JSON text directly.
Import preset from clipboard. Make sure you have copied a valid Canta preset JSON.
Change the name and description of this preset.
Create a preset from currently uninstalled apps. This will save a list of apps that can be shared and applied on other devices.
Create or import presets to manage app uninstall lists across devices
Grant permission to Canta in Shizuku
Canta uses Shizuku to uninstall apps without requiring root access. Shizuku provides a secure way to access system-level SDKs.
Where to get commit info for updates from
Where to get badges and descriptions from.
Whether to allow selecting apps marked as unsafe (applying presets bypasses this already).
Enjoying Canta? It\'s built in my free time with privacy in mind - no ads, no tracking. If you find it useful, please consider supporting its development!
Hides the success dialog after uninstall / reinstall.
Require authentication for uninstalling or reinstalling apps.
Choose which Android device Canta should manage. Enable USB debugging on the device and authorize this computer when prompted.
No devices found. Check the connection and try again.
Connect your Android device over USB, then pick it in the browser prompt. Enable USB debugging on the device and accept the authorization prompt on its screen.
This browser cannot access USB devices. Open Canta in Chromium based browser (e.g. Chrome, Brave, Edge, Vivaldi) on a computer to connect your phone.
Access to the USB device was denied. Unplug it and plug it back in, grant access again with \"Pick device\", and make sure no other program (such as adb) is using the device.

Access to the USB device was denied. On Linux, browsers need permission to open USB devices: install udev rules for your phone (e.g. the android-udev-rules package), then unplug it and plug it back in.
Access to the USB device was denied. On Windows, the phone\'s ADB interface needs a WinUSB driver: install it with Zadig, then unplug the phone and plug it back in.
Could not connect to the device: %1$s
The selected device is no longer available. Please pick it again.
The device is already in use by another program or browser tab. Close anything else using it, unplug the device and plug it back in, then pick it again.

The device is busy: another program on this computer has claimed it. On Linux this is often ModemManager, an adb server, or a file-transfer (MTP) monitor. Stop them (e.g. sudo systemctl stop ModemManager), unplug the phone and plug it back in, then pick it again.
